Use cases, document formats, extraction requirements, structured facts, unstructured passages and an MCP-client query planner.

29 October 2026Target: Sangrail/testEnvironment: macOS POCStatus: design notes, not implemented specification
01 / Purpose and premise

The question drives what we extract

An engineering lead should be able to ask ordinary-language questions across a project-organised portfolio of engineering files, receive an accurate answer or document list, and see precisely what source evidence made each result relevant.

The initial repository is a filesystem, probably organised by project. Files may include engineering reports, specifications, drawings, CAD assemblies, schedules and compliance records. The eventual corpus could comprise terabytes of material, spanning years of formats and revisions, with no reliable file-type distribution known in advance. The filesystem is the source of truth. Searchable databases and indexes are derived artefacts, not replacement document repositories.

Product promise

Ask without knowing the file

“Which projects contain S355 steel components whose allowable distributed loads fall below 5 kN/m², and where is that specified?” The system should discover the relevant records, not demand that the engineer knows filenames or SQL.

Engineering obligation

Show why, not merely what

Every match must resolve to a parent document and immutable version, with the page, table, cell, text span or CAD entity that supports it. A citation establishes provenance; it is not proof that an extracted interpretation is correct.

The design rule: questions → needed evidence → file-format/reader capability → canonical extracted information → appropriate indexes → permission-safe query plan → cited result. We must not assume that vector search or a single generic text extractor can answer every engineering question.

Scope and constraints as agreed

DimensionStarting constraintConsequence
RepositoryExisting folders and files, potentially very large and project-organised.Inventory first; incremental, idempotent extraction; retain original paths and hashes.
File heterogeneityUnknown mix of PDF, text, tables, CAD/BIM and proprietary formats; versions may differ.Detect by content, version and capability; register tested readers; report gaps honestly.
AccessDifferent users can read different folders/files.Authorisation before ranking, limits and SQL aggregation; recheck at evidence/document open.
Local prototypemacOS and simulated login/permissions now; Windows identity and ACL integration later.Keep a replaceable authorisation interface, without implying the mock is secure.
SearchExact identifiers, numeric constraints, material codes, compliance status and semantic topics.Structured SQL plus BM25/keyword search; vectors only where evaluation justifies them.
PlanningThe LLM lives in the MCP host/client and decides which tools to call.Discoverable safe schema and bounded SQL tools. No extra server-side planning LLM required.
EvidenceEvery result needs a reason and original document location.Source identifiers and extraction lineage are first-class records.
02 / Starting position

What we have, and what we are proposing

This section records the public state of Sangrail/test as documented on 29 October 2026. It is a snapshot of the existing MVP, not a claim about later local Codex changes. The repository itself should be checked again before implementation.

138
Curated indexed test files, not a real enterprise corpus
2
Content families indexed today: Markdown and text-layer PDF
FTS5
Existing SQLite passage inverted index and BM25 ranking
2
Existing MCP tools: search_evidence and read_evidence

The fixture tree includes 120 generated Markdown project files, 10 Project Cedar Markdown reviews, three Markdown specifications, synthetic PDF reports/registers, and two public FHWA PDF references. These files were assembled for testing; they do not represent the actual distribution of CAD versions, spreadsheets, scanned documents or enterprise permissions.

Documented current MVP

What exists

Python service, web UI, simulated users and folder rules, SQLite documents/passages/FTS5 indexes, SHA-256 source identity, page/line evidence, audit logging, heuristic answer selection and a local stdio MCP server.

The web and MCP processes share index files but each creates its own service instance.

Desired extension

What is not yet established

Content/version-aware reader registry, PDF table cells and spreadsheet extraction, structured engineering fact store, robust CAD/JT parsing, capability-level coverage, permission-scoped SQL, schema-discovery MCP tools, and optional semantic embeddings.

These are design goals, not existing capabilities in the public MVP.

Current physical and logical organisation

Source folders in the test repository are heterogeneous. Project identity is often inferred from a path rather than a dedicated project record. The following is a representative future folder organisation, not a listing of the actual repository.

The current SQLite content index is documented as follows. This is as-built rather than the proposed engineering ontology.

Current tablePurpose
documentsPath, SHA-256 file version and passage count.
passagesText, heading, PDF page, line range.
passages_ftsFTS5 search over heading, text, path words.
metaLast index modification metadata.

Separate SQLite stores/records support jobs and audit. There is no authoritative structured engineering facts table in the documented MVP.

Existing defects that affect the new plan

The public architecture document describes several correctness gaps that should be resolved before results are treated as reliable: a roof-load question may select a floor-load value from the same document; numerical matching may lose negative signs; permission filtering and folder scoping occur after a 1,000-passage candidate limit; a scanned PDF without text can be reported as indexed; a file-read error can stop refresh; and independent web/MCP refreshes can race. These are reported defects, not merely future features.

03 / Question catalogue

Sample questions, required evidence and retrieval type

The question catalogue is the acceptance-test seed. Each example describes the data the indexer must extract, and the store or algorithm best suited to the final predicate. A “mention” is not interchangeable with a requirement, permission, measured value or approved state.

ID / categoryQuestion the engineer asksRequired extracted evidenceRetrieval pattern

Numeric		Which beams have a specified allowable distributed load below 5 kN/m²?Beam ID, property role “allowable capacity”, numeric value, original unit, SI value, source row/cell, revision.Typed SQL threshold and dimensional validation.
Q02
Unit precision		Which components have loads below 5 N/m²?Same as Q01, but a threshold of 5 N/m², not 5 kN/m².SQL. Never silently multiply the query by 1,000.
Q03

Q05

Q06

Q07
Concept		Find reports discussing fatigue and corrosion in marine structures.Headings, paragraphs, terms, conceptual context, page and passage.FTS5/BM25 now; optional vector search later.
Q08

Q09

Q10

Q11
Absence		Which projects lack an approved material certificate for a specified component?Expected components/certificates, their relationships, approval evidence, extraction coverage.Coverage-aware NOT EXISTS; never assert global absence from partial ingestion.
Q12
Multi-predicate		Find S355 components under 5 kN/m² in projects awaiting approval.Material and load tied to the same component, project status and evidence.SQL joins and evidence lookup; optionally text search.

All example project names, files and material/load rows in this design note are illustrative unless explicitly identified as existing repository fixture values. “Approved” must refer to an identified authority or source; a text mention of approval is not by itself a verified workflow state.

One concrete extraction test

Imagine a PDF report or Excel schedule with the following source table. The values below are synthetic examples to exercise the extraction contract.

ComponentMaterialProperty (source header)ValueRevision
B-104S355Allowable UDL4.5 kN/m²C
B-105S355Allowable UDL6.0 kN/m²C
F-021C30/37Imposed design load3.2 kN/m²B

For Q12, B-104 qualifies on material and load; B-105 fails the threshold; F-021 must not qualify because both its material and its engineering property differ. The important structural fact is that columns across a single source row refer to a single component. Flattening these cells into a document-sized text blob destroys that binding.

04 / Format-sensitive ingestion

The same question meets different kinds of files

We do not yet know which formats or source versions dominate the real portfolio. The discovery pass must therefore inventory every file, including files that cannot be parsed. The extension is only a hint: content signatures and format-specific headers determine what we believe a file actually contains.

File familyInformation that may hold answersRequired extraction and locatorBaseline / caveat
Markdown / textNotes, specifications, plain-text tables, revision comments.Headings, paragraphs, Markdown table rows/cells; line ranges and section names.MVP text Table structure is a proposed extension.
PDF, selectable textReports, calculations, embedded schedules, annotations, approval tables.Text blocks with page/line, layout-aware tables with page/bounding box/row/column; layout confidence.MVP text pypdf text extraction exists; robust table cells not yet established.
PDF, scanned/mixedPhotocopied drawings, stamped approvals, image-only tables.Page-image classification, OCR/layout/table recognition with coordinates and quality scores.Gap No OCR currently; mixed pages require partial status.
CSV / XLSXMaterial schedules, load registers, cross-project approvals, formulas and units.Workbook/sheet, header/row/column, cell address, raw value, typed value, formula and units.Planned Formula caches may be missing or stale.
DOCXSpecifications, tables, approvals, tracked/revised text.Paragraphs, tables/cells, headings, document metadata, stable locator when possible.Profile first
IFC / BIMBuilding element properties, classifications, material assignments, quantities.Object GUID/type, property sets, relationships, units; element/global ID.Reader validation
DXF / DWG / DGNTitle blocks, layers, blocks, entity attributes, tables, external references.Sheet/layout, attribute/tag, entity handle, xref, original CAD version.Version-dependent DXF may be easier than proprietary DWG/DGN.
JTAssembly hierarchy, parts, attributes, tessellations, PMI and sometimes B-rep.Version-bearing header; reader compatibility; entity/assembly path/PMI locator if a verified reader extracts it.No verified reader A JT header probe is not JT geometry extraction.
STEP / CATIA / NX / RVTAssemblies, engineering metadata, components, material/classification properties.Native object identities, relationship paths, metadata and geometry only where supported.Capabilities unknown Test actual file versions and licences.
Images / archives / unknownScans, diagrams, packaged projects, embedded reference files.OCR or safe package inventory; provenance to member/source; failure status.Inventory first Do not silently invent readable content.

Reader selection must include the file version

Discover
all paths
→
Detect
format + version
→
Probe
reader capability
→
Extract
with locations
→
Report
coverage + gaps

A reader manifest should state its own version, supported source-format versions, platform, dependencies, licence, and which capabilities it can extract: metadata, text, tables, properties, geometry and PMI. The extraction attempt then records what actually worked, not merely what the manifest promised.

JT example: a file ending in .jt is discovered. We inspect a bounded header and determine whether it appears to be JT, what version it reports, and how confident the detection is. We then ask the reader registry whether any installed, licensed, platform-compatible and tested adapter can extract the requested information from that version. A detected but unreadable file remains in the inventory as NO_READER, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, or another precise status. It is not “fully indexed”. JT version/header inspection is only a detector-level capability, not proof that geometry, properties or PMI have been parsed.

Deterministic extraction before interpretation

Native fields, workbook cells, CAD properties and correctly parsed tables should be extracted by deterministic readers first. Engineering dictionaries and unit parsers can then normalise common properties and references. Model-assisted extraction is reserved for ambiguous prose, poorly structured documents or difficult visual layouts, and every proposed fact must be grounded in exact source evidence.

05 / Data we need to retain

One source document, several connected representations

The indexer should emit a canonical extraction envelope for each immutable document version. From it, we can build a structured SQL representation and an unstructured passage index without losing common source identity and location.

File + version
hash · path · ACL scope
→
Reader result
blocks · tables · entities
→
Normalisation
units · roles · subjects
Structured representation / SQL
  • Projects, documents and versions
  • Table headers, rows and cells
  • Engineering objects and typed assertions
  • Materials, loads, statuses and edges
Unstructured representation / retrieval
  • Paragraphs, passages and annotations
  • Headings, context and text spans
  • FTS5 / BM25 index
  • Optional evaluated embeddings
↓ shared document and evidence IDs ↓
Authorised evidence-backed answer

Proposed minimum canonical entities

Logical entityFields that matterWhy it exists
source_filesRoot/path, project candidate, extension, size, timestamps, fingerprint, content family/version.Inventory including files no reader can open.
documents / document_versionsLogical ID, source ID, SHA-256, revision, effective/superseded state, path, identity.Separate “the document” from an immutable version of its bytes.
reader_attemptsDetector, detected version, selected reader/version, capabilities, elapsed time, error codes.Measure partial extraction, unsupported versions and failures.
content_blocksType, text, heading, page/line, bounding box, sheet or CAD locator.Original passage evidence and unstructured retrieval.
source_tables / source_rows / source_cellsTable ID, headers, row/column IDs, source/value types, original text, coordinates.Preserve which values belong together and where they came from.
engineering_objectsProject, component/assembly ID, category, stable native ID if available.Bind properties to beams, floors, parts and assemblies, not merely whole files.
factsSubject, canonical property, assertion role, original/typed value, SI unit, qualifiers, evidence ID.Exact numeric, material and status queries.
relationshipsSource, target, type, time/revision, evidence.Project-to-document, component-to-material, reference and supersession joins.
extraction_coveragePer-capability success/partial/none/unsupported, warnings and last attempt.Truthful reporting of what can and cannot be searched.

Example: one source row becomes a typed assertion

Sourceloads.xlsx
Components!D27
Revision C
→
Canonical factB-104 · allowable UDL
4.5 kN/m² → 4500 N/m²
→
ResultDocument + sheet/cell
why it matches < 5 kN/m²

A fact must distinguish design demand from allowable capacity, and a proposed specification from an inspection measurement or a prohibited material. Preserve original wording, dimensional unit, signs, ranges, tolerance, extraction method, source revision and confidence. The canonical code allowable_distributed_load should not be equated with every mention of “load”.

{ "document_version_id": "doc-A@sha256:…", "evidence": {
    "format": "xlsx", "sheet": "Components", "cell": "D27",
    "row_id": "row-27", "original_text": "4.5 kN/m²" },
  "subject": { "type": "beam", "id": "B-104" },
  "property": "allowable_distributed_load",
  "assertion_role": "design_specification",
  "value": { "original": 4.5, "unit": "kN/m²",
             "normalised": 4500, "unit_si": "N/m²" },
  "extraction": { "method": "deterministic_table",
                  "reader": "xlsx-reader", "verified": false } }

Proposed record only. The row identity, column header and file version let the user confirm that the value is attached to the right component and source. Never return this example as if it were evidence from the live repository.

06 / Query and retrieval

The MCP host’s LLM is the query planner

The MCP server exposes tools; the language model in the MCP client/host chooses how to combine them. There is no need to insert a second server-side model purely to translate natural language to SQL. A web search can continue to use the existing deterministic interface; a conversational planner in the web UI is a separate, future decision.

Current

Search already available

FTS5/BM25 over passages, answer heuristics, search_evidence and read_evidence through the local MCP server. These must remain functional during the migration.

Proposed tools

Schema-aware planning

list_tables, describe_schema, describe_table, query_sql, search_documents and get_document_evidence, with appropriate privilege checks.

A natural-language question becomes an executable plan

For “Find S355 components with allowable distributed loads below 5 kN/m² in projects awaiting approval”, the client should discover the schema, recognise a structured join and numeric predicate, request evidence for the authorised matches and return cited source rows. For “find reports discussing corrosion in saline environments”, it should use text retrieval, potentially combined with a semantic index if that is later introduced and measured.

MCP host LLM
parse intent
→
Describe schema
keys · units · joins
→
Choose tool(s)
SQL / FTS / vector
→
Verify results
evidence + permissions
-- Illustrative only; proposed schema, not current MVP SQL.
SELECT d.document_id, d.path, f.subject_id,
       f.value_number_si, f.evidence_id
FROM allowed_facts AS f
JOIN allowed_documents AS d
  ON d.document_version_id = f.document_version_id
WHERE f.property_code = 'allowable_distributed_load'
  AND f.assertion_role = 'design_specification'
  AND f.dimension_code = 'pressure'
  AND f.value_number_si < 5000;

Important: the allowed_* names above denote a server-controlled, permission-scoped read-only projection. They are not an instruction to let a model invent tables or execute unrestricted SQL against the main index. Any mixed query joining materials and load properties must enforce that they refer to the same engineering object or verified source row.

Exact identifiers and material grades generally suit lexical matching or structured filters. Numeric comparisons need typed SQL. BM25 answers vocabulary-based questions. Embeddings can improve concept retrieval but should remain an evaluated optional layer, not an automatic prerequisite. Hybrid ranking must never override mandatory structured constraints.

07 / Access and trustworthy evidence

Permission safety and source traceability are system properties

On macOS, the POC simulates a user identity and folder/file access rules. The public fixture describes users JP, Kamal and Maya; the local MCP process uses a --user selection that is not authenticated. The simulated model demonstrates filtering behaviour, not a secure production identity boundary.

Permission invariant

Authorise before candidates become results

A user must see only the documents and dependent facts they can access. Apply authorisation before top-K, pagination, counts, joins, aggregates, reranking and evidence fetch. Recheck when opening the parent source. An unauthorised document must not influence visible counts or displacement of relevant results.

Production boundary

Authentication is replaceable

Future Windows deployment can integrate verified enterprise identity and NTFS/SMB effective-access semantics, including groups, inheritance and deny rules. Windows login alone does not guarantee that a Python service’s file reads occur under that user's effective access token.

An acceptable result contract

Result fieldUser-visible meaning
Document identity and titleWhich authoritative parent file contains the match.
Immutable versionWhich exact file revision/bytes were indexed, usually hash plus revision metadata.
Evidence excerpt and locatorExact source text/cell, PDF page/box, workbook sheet/cell, or CAD entity reference.
Why matchedPredicate, matched property/value, exact spec code or semantic passage relevance.
Trust and coverage stateDeterministic/model-derived, verified/unverified, and whether the source was partly extracted.
Permissions and freshnessAccess checked for this user; source not silently replaced by a newer version.

Negative findings are conditional: “no documents found” only means no match in the portion of the authorised, successfully indexed corpus covered by the selected retrieval mechanisms. It does not establish that the document or requirement does not exist in unreadable JT files, scanned PDFs, unsupported formats or inaccessible project folders. The LLM's prose is a presentation of the tool output, not an independent source of proof.

08 / Failures and extraction gaps

The unreadable corpus must be visible

Extraction is not binary. A JT header can be recognised while its geometry remains opaque; a PDF may yield paragraphs but no schedule cells; an XLSX workbook may reveal headers but contain formulas without usable cached values. Those are distinct capability outcomes, and each should be persisted for every reader attempt.

Outcome classExamplesWhat the system must say
INDEXED_FULLAll required capabilities for this file’s target extraction profile succeeded.Which capabilities were in scope and verified.
INDEXED_PARTIALPDF text extracted but tables broken; some pages OCR-only; partial workbook.What was searchable and what remains missing.
UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT / UNSUPPORTED_VERSIONUnknown proprietary type; JT version has no matching reader.Detected format/version and nearest known capability gap.
NO_READER / DEPENDENCY_MISSING / LICENCE_UNAVAILABLEReader manifest exists but cannot run on this Mac or is not installed/licensed.What dependency or tested reader is needed.
NO_TEXT_LAYER / ENCRYPTEDScanned PDF or inaccessible password-protected PDF.OCR/decryption needed; no false claim of a complete index.
READ_ERROR / TIMEOUT / READER_CRASHDamaged file, permission error, hung native CAD parser.Isolated file failure, attempt metadata and safe retry hint.
FORMAT_MISMATCH.jt extension with non-JT signature.Content detection conflict; do not trust extension alone.

The coverage dashboard should report counts and bytes by detected family/version, full/partial/unsupported/failed state, reader ID/version, capabilities achieved, tables/rows/facts extracted, and affected projects. Queryable coverage is particularly important for compliance and missing-evidence questions.

{ "path": "Project_A/01_Design/assembly.jt",
  "detected_format": "jt", "detected_version": "10.x",
  "detector_result": "header_only",
  "reader_id": null, "status": "NO_READER",
  "capabilities": {
    "metadata": "header_only", "text": "unsupported",
    "tables": "unsupported", "geometry": "unsupported",
    "pmi": "unsupported" },
  "issue_code": "JT_READER_NOT_VERIFIED" }

Diagnostic illustration only. The version shown is a placeholder, not a report from a real JT source file.

09 / Decisions and early priorities

How we should proceed from this baseline

The first useful deliverable is not a more elaborate chatbot. It is a trustworthy inventory showing what is present, which versions are readable, what was actually extracted and how that evidence maps to the questions above. The query planner can only be as reliable as the source representations available to it.

OrderIncrementObservable acceptance condition
01Audit and correctness baselineExisting web/MCP behaviour retained; known wrong-parameter, signed-value and pre-authorisation-limit errors tested and addressed.
02Full file inventory, content/version detection and reader registryEvery file inventoried; unknown JT version or missing reader reported with a reason; one failure never aborts its neighbours.
03Canonical extraction and source-linked tablesMarkdown, PDF table, CSV and XLSX sample files produce columns, rows, cells and precise source locators.
04Typed engineering facts and relationshipsCorrect subject/property/role/units, project links, version and approval claims; test rows return accurate values.
05Permission-scoped SQL and MCP schema discoveryClient LLM discovers allowed schema and runs restricted SQL; all counts, joins, ranking and evidence obey access policy.
06Coverage-aware UI and evaluationEvery result shows why it matched; the admin view exposes format/version gaps and false negatives due to incomplete extraction.

Questions we have not answered yet

We still need a representative profile of the actual corpus, including formats, versions, file age, size and location of important parameters. We also need the authoritative source of project compliance status, the document/revision identification scheme, a business definition of “current”, the acceptable data egress policy for an external LLM, and the permitted CAD reader technologies and licences. These are discovery tasks, not reasons to invent premature architecture.

Starting-point conclusion: the corpus and the questions jointly determine extraction strategy. The index is a set of evidence-preserving projections over source files: structured facts for exact engineering conditions, passages for language-based discovery, reader and coverage records for reliability, and a shared policy boundary for every user and MCP client.
